import ctypes
import math

# Load the required libraries in correct order
cblas = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgslcblas.so", mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
gsl = ctypes.CDLL("/usr/local/gsl/lib/libgsl.so")

# Define the function signature
gsl.gsl_expm1.argtypes = [ctypes.c_double]
gsl.gsl_expm1.restype = ctypes.c_double

def gsl_expm1_py(x):
    return gsl.gsl_expm1(x)

def assert_test():
    # Test with small values where Taylor series is used
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(0.0), 0.0, abs_tol=1e-15)
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(0.001), math.expm1(0.001), rel_tol=1e-14)
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(-0.001), math.expm1(-0.001), rel_tol=1e-14)
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(0.5), math.expm1(0.5), rel_tol=1e-14)
    
    # Test with larger values where exp(x)-1 is used
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(1.0), math.expm1(1.0), rel_tol=1e-14)
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(-1.0), math.expm1(-1.0), rel_tol=1e-14)
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(10.0), math.expm1(10.0), rel_tol=1e-14)
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(-10.0), math.expm1(-10.0), rel_tol=1e-14)
    
    # Test edge cases
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(1e-10), math.expm1(1e-10), rel_tol=1e-14)
    assert math.isclose(gsl_expm1_py(-1e-10), math.expm1(-1e-10), rel_tol=1e-14)
    
    print("All tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert_test()
